novelty.justification: The claim’s novelty route is a specific mechanistic relationship: the model allegedly “first retrieves the affirmative fact using the same mid-layer machinery as the positive query” and applies a “late, shallow, and error-prone” negation override, with failures caused by persistence of the affirmative direction. Searches using “LLM negation mechanistic interpretability,” “negation affirmative retrieval late layer suppression,” “transformer negation activation patching,” and “LLM ironic negation forbidden token circuits” found the closest work to be “Don’t Think of the White Bear: Ironic Negation in Transformer Models Under Cognitive Load” (2025), which already proposes that suppression requires activating the forbidden concept and reports circuit-level layer dynamics; “When Truth Is Overridden” (2025) likewise identifies late-layer override of factual knowledge in sycophancy. Extending these established activation-then-suppression and knowledge-override accounts specifically to parametric factual retrieval is a substantive operationalization with a new error decomposition, but it is a natural extension rather than a wholly new core paradigm, while subtracting an answer direction is a standard activation-steering adaptation.
